utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue, I'd first like to deliver a decision, that is, a decision of the Chamber giving the reasons for its decision delivered yesterday on closed session for Witness 666. In a decision of the 1st of September, 2004, the witness was already granted protective measures in the form of a pseudonym, image and voice distortion, and private session for those portions of his testimony reasonably likely to reveal his identity. During yesterday's session, the witness stated that "the maximum level of protection" was in fact what he had in mind when communicating his security concerns to the Prosecution. He also expressed additional concerns with regards to the safety of family members and argued that the protective measures already granted would not be sufficient. The Chamber will not reiterate the reasons for granting protective measures for Witness 666, as they were set out in the decision of the 1st of September last year. The present decision only concerns the degree of protection, not the need for protective measures. The Chamber must be satisfied that protective measures less restrictive than those sought would not address the security concerns of the witness. The Chamber has considered the arguments of the parties, the submissions by the witness, and its own decision of the 1st of September, 2004. The Chamber finds that given the position of the witness, the nature of his testimony, as clarified during yesterday's session, would, of itself, allow him to be identified. Moreover, having now read the transcripts of the interviews the Prosecution has held with the witness, the Chamber finds it most likely that under the previous protective measures regime, most, if not all of the witness's testimony, would have required private session. The Chamber considers that the risk that the witness would be identified through small portions of his testimony given in open session is not outweighed by the advantages of these small portions of testimony being heard in open session. The Chamber considers therefore that there is a need for him to testify in closed session. This concludes the Chamber's reasoning for the decision on closed session for Witness 666. I further have another procedural matter I'd like to briefly raise. We did lose some time yesterday. The Chamber has prepared arrangements for a prolonged hearing next Friday. That would mean that we would also sit part or whole of the afternoon. The Chamber wants to announce that and to hear if any of the parties would find major problems, not in general terms - specific terms - for next Friday to be present at that hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour means Friday this week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This week, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: May I ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, "next Friday," I know that it's always a problem. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry. I just wanted to be clear, Your Honour. I don't think it matters particularly which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I was first up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to say that no, it doesn't -- it doesn't present problems to the Defence in this sense that actually, Your Honour, on our side we feel reasonably confident that this session actually won't be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It would require a little bit of reorganisation on our side if it did, Your Honour, and we would cope with that, but that's our position at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stewart. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We were consulted in advance, as was Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And we appreciate the Court's efforts. That scheduling is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then are there any other procedural matters to be raised at this moment before we continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, yes, Your Honour. Just a very small point. Your Honour, we've got witnesses 31 and 555 coming up, is it? I can't remember exactly the status on protective measures. I know at least one of them is subject to protective measures. I'll just say the numbers. Witness 31 tomorrow and Witness 555 due on Friday. Your Honour, the Defence has in mind that unless there is some problem or difficulty, that both those witnesses would be taken by Mr. Josse. And I hope that the Trial Chamber is content with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although the Chamber would prefer to be in a position where it wouldn't need any decision any more to have Mr. Josse take the witness, the Chamber accepts that and will further inquire into the development of talks between the Registry and the Defence and Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's a bigger topic which I won't address this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I just want to emphasise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. And I have some further inquiries and information to explore there about where exactly we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But that's another topic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do I understand. But I would like to make one observation in this respect. For tomorrow, a videolink witness is scheduled; I think it's Witness 31. That is difficult to move, so therefore whatever happens we'll start anyhow with the videolink witness tomorrow, even if we're not finished with the witness of today, because we can't change that easily the videolink. This is just to inform the parties. Of course, we do not know to what extent it's necessary, but for scheduling purposes you should be aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that was going to be my -- my next request and happily Your Honours have completely anticipated and that fits in entirely with what I was going to request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So I have nothing more to say now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No further matters to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No. We're ready to call the next witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of July, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.05 p.m.,
